memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Jacob awoke from his sleep, he thought, 'Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was not aware of it.' He was afraid and said, 'How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven.'" - Gen 28:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob wakes with a jolt of realisation: "Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was not aware of it." He had lain down thinking he was utterly alone in an empty wilderness. But God had been there all along. Jacob's problem was not God's absence — it was his own unawareness.

How often is that our situation too? We move through our days feeling that God is far off, that we are facing life alone. Yet the truth is that God is present in places we least expect — in the ordinary, the difficult, even the lonely wilderness. We are simply "not aware of it." Our sense of His absence is often a failure of perception, not a fact of reality.

Jacob's response is holy fear and wonder: "How awesome is this place! This is the gate of heaven." Once he realised God was near, everything changed. An ordinary patch of ground became sacred simply because God was there.

May God open our eyes to His nearness. He is with His people always, even when we do not feel Him. The dull commute, the hospital room, the quiet kitchen, the sleepless night — these can all become "the house of God" when we awaken to the truth that He is here. Ask the Lord to make you aware of the presence you may have been missing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might God be present that I have failed to notice?
2. Do I move through life assuming God is far, when He is near?
3. How would my ordinary places change if I saw them as "the house of God"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for the times I have felt alone when You were with me all along. Open my eyes to Your nearness and make me aware of Your presence today. Amen.
